children: Indonesia's financial regulator has issued a rule on the country's stock exchange, paving the way for the planned demutualisation of the exchange, local media Kontan reported on Sunday.
The demutualisation means turning the exchange into a public entity owned by shareholders, rather than the member-controlled, self-regulating organisation it is currently.
The rule allows Indonesia's finance ministry, Bank Indonesia and Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara to hold shares in the exchange, Kontan news site reported.
The financial regulator did not immediately respond to request for confirmation.
Parties may hold up to 5% without the regulator approval, while larger stakes above 5% require approval and no shareholder may control more than 50%, Kontan reported.
Individual investors may only acquire the exchange shares through a public offering, Kontan added.
It is part of stock exchange reform plan following a market rout earlier this year, which raised concerns over governance and transparency.
